transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi! So, um, I came in because I feel like I just cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Like, my supplies, my due dates, receipts, assignment notes... they all just end up in these giant piles. 

I actually make resin keychains and stuff for the shop, and I just bought this really amazing holographic glitter online. The shipping was incredibly fast, which is so weird because usually the post office takes forever, right? Last time I ordered from them, they sent my package to the completely wrong state, and I had to spend like an hour on hold with customer service just listening to that awful elevator music. 

But anyway, yeah, everything for school and the shop is just in piles everywhere in my room, and I just stand there looking at it all and I honestly don't know what to do first.
How stressful does it feel for you to be surrounded by these piles of schoolwork and shop supplies?

Um, honestly? I'm not really sure. I don't know if I'd say it's stressful, exactly, because I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess I just kind of stare at it. 

Like, the other day I was digging through the pile on my desk to find a shipping receipt, and I actually found this old mood ring I bought at a street fair when I was like, twelve. Do you remember those? The ones that turn blue when you're happy and black when you're stressed? Mine was just stuck on green, which is supposed to mean 'calm' or something, but honestly I think the heat-sensitive stuff inside it just broke because I accidentally left it in my mom's car over the summer. Her car gets so incredibly hot because the AC has been broken for years, and she refuses to get it fixed because she says the mechanic always tries to upsell her on windshield wipers. Which is true, they totally do! Every single time she goes in for an oil change. 

But yeah, wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, the piles. Yeah, I don't know exactly how it makes me feel, just... I don't really know.
Do you find it hard to focus on one task for a long time?

Oh, totally. Like, if I'm in a class or watching one of those instructional videos for my business assignments, I can start out listening just fine. But after a few minutes, my mind is completely on new charm designs or order ideas. 

Actually, speaking of charms, I just found this amazing supplier online who makes these tiny little miniature boba tea cups. They are so incredibly cute, they even have little fake tapioca pearls in the bottom! I want to make them into earrings, but my friend Sarah said chunky earrings are getting too heavy and people want lighter stuff now. Sarah actually just got her cartilage pierced last week, and she totally fainted right there at the mall! The guy doing the piercing didn't even know what to do, he just ran over and bought her a pretzel from Auntie Anne's. Have you had their cinnamon sugar pretzels? They are literally the best thing ever, especially when they're fresh out of the oven and all warm. 

But wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, focusing on things. Yeah, so I'll be thinking about the boba charms or my shop orders, and then I look back at the screen and realize I completely missed half of what the video or the teacher actually said.
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities for school or your shop due to your difficulties with organization and focus?

Yeah, it's actually getting pretty bad. Because of all this, I totally missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is at risk. Which is honestly terrifying because dealing with the financial aid office is the worst. They use this online portal that makes you change your password every single month, and I always write it on a pink sticky note, but then my cat Barnaby—he's this massive orange tabby—he literally eats paper. I found half of my last password note floating in his water bowl! He’s so weird about water. Like, whenever someone takes a shower, he just sits in the empty bathtub staring at the drain for hours. My mom says he's hunting ghosts, but she watches way too many of those paranormal investigation shows on cable. Have you seen the one where they go to the abandoned lighthouses? It's so obviously fake, but I completely binge-watched it last weekend. 

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, my responsibilities. Yeah, so the school thing is a huge mess. And then with the shop, the people I usually work with on projects have totally started depending on me less. They just don't really ask me to collaborate as much anymore because I keep losing track of things. Which reminds me, my friend who does the resin molds with me just bought a new pressure pot to get the air bubbles out of the plastic, and it looks exactly like a giant Instant Pot! I love Instant Pots, you can make mac and cheese in like ten minutes... but yeah, I guess my responsibilities are definitely kind of falling apart right now.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?

Yeah, I definitely do that. Like, especially in group critiques for my art projects or during class discussions, I'll just jump right in with my answer before the other person is even done talking. I just get so excited or I think I know exactly where they're going with it, but then I feel so embarrassed because I realize I just guessed what they were going to say and completely cut them off. 

It actually happened last week in my ceramics critique. This girl was talking about the glaze on my mug, and I just blurted out that I used the wrong firing temperature before she even finished her sentence. Speaking of ceramics, I am so obsessed with this new speckled clay we're using. It has these tiny little flecks in it that look like vanilla bean ice cream when it's fired. Oh my gosh, have you tried the vanilla bean at that local dairy place down the street? They make their waffle cones fresh right in front of you, and the smell is literally incredible. It smells exactly like this candle I bought at Target, which I actually left burning in my room once by accident and my mom freaked out. She bought me one of those wax warmers instead, but it's shaped like an owl and the eyes glow red when it's on, which is honestly kind of creepy when you're trying to sleep. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, interrupting people. Yeah, I do that a lot in class and then I just feel super awkward about it.
Do you feel like your difficulties with organization and focus are causing you a lot of distress?

Um, distress? I mean, I don't know if I'd call it distress, exactly. Like, it's annoying, for sure, especially the school stuff, but I wouldn't say I'm, like, falling apart crying over it. I don't really think about it that much unless something bad happens, like the financial aid thing. 

Actually, speaking of crying, my friend Jessica was just crying the other day because she dropped her brand new phone right on the pavement. The screen completely shattered, it looked like a spiderweb. She had just bought this super cute phone case for it, too—it had these little pressed flowers inside the clear plastic. I tried making phone cases like that once with resin, but the flowers always turned brown. You have to dry them in silica gel first, apparently. I bought a huge tub of silica gel on Amazon, but the delivery guy left it out in the rain and the box totally disintegrated. Have you ever tried to pick up a wet cardboard box? It just turns to mush in your hands. It's so gross. 

But yeah, anyway, what were we saying? Distress? Um, no, I don't think I'm really that distressed about it. It's just kind of frustrating sometimes.
Are your difficulties with organization, focus, and interrupting others causing problems in your relationships with friends or family?

Um, relationships? Like, with my friends and family? I don't really think so. I mean, my mom gets annoyed with me sometimes when I leave my stuff everywhere, but we don't, like, have huge fights about it. And my friends are all pretty chill. Actually, my friend Maya—she's the one who does the resin stuff with me—she's so chill she literally fell asleep during a concert once. It was a punk rock show, too! The bass was so loud you could feel it vibrating in your chest, but she just sat down against a speaker and passed out. I wish I could sleep like that. I always need it to be completely silent and pitch black, which is why I bought these blackout curtains for my room. But I didn't measure the window right, so they're like two feet too short and the sun just blasts me right in the face at 6 AM anyway. I tried using a sleep mask, but I always rip it off in the middle of the night without realizing it. I found it under my bed once, completely covered in dust bunnies. Dust bunnies are so weird, right? Like, how does dust even form into a bunny shape? 

Wait, sorry. Relationships, right? Yeah, no, I haven't really noticed it causing any big problems with anyone. Just normal stuff, I guess.
Are you having trouble keeping up with your schoolwork or managing your shop because of these organizational issues and difficulties with focus?

Yeah, it’s definitely causing some trouble. Like, because of all this, I actually missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is completely at risk. The financial aid office is in this building that has the weirdest architecture, by the way—it literally looks like a giant concrete waffle. Speaking of waffles, I tried to make some on Sunday but I totally forgot to use cooking spray, and the batter basically cemented itself to the iron. I was scraping it for like twenty minutes with a butter knife before I just gave up and ate dry cereal. Have you ever noticed how weird the texture of dry Frosted Flakes is? It's like eating sweet glass. My dentist always yells at me about eating too much sugar, but his waiting room has those really good strawberry candies with the soft centers in a glass bowl, so it’s kind of sending mixed messages, you know? 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, schoolwork and the shop! Yeah, so the financial aid thing is really bad. And then with the shop projects, I’ve noticed the people I work with have started depending on me way less. Like, they just don't trust me to handle the important parts of the assignments anymore, which sucks. We're supposed to be building this big wooden frame together, and they basically just gave me the sandpaper and told me to stay in the corner. Sandpaper is so weirdly satisfying though, isn't it? The grit feels exactly like a cat's tongue. My aunt has a hairless cat and it feels like a warm peach when you pet it, but it always tries to sit on my laptop keyboard when I'm typing... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question again? Did I answer the thing about the shop?
Are you having trouble keeping up with your daily responsibilities or maintaining relationships because of your organizational issues and difficulties with focus?

Um, daily responsibilities? Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I think I just mentioned this, but because of all this stuff, I completely missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is totally at risk. Which is super stressful, honestly. I've been trying to call them, but their hold music is that same classical song that plays in every elevator ever. It's like, dun dun dun... I think it's Mozart? Or maybe Bach. I always get them confused. My middle school music teacher was obsessed with Bach, he even had a bust of him on his piano. It was made of this weird fake marble that was always freezing cold. I tried to put a tiny knitted hat on it once during winter because it looked so sad, but Mr. Henderson got so mad at me. He had this vein in his forehead that would literally throb when he yelled. 

Oh, right, but anyway—so yeah, the financial aid thing. And then with relationships... well, like I said about the shop projects, the people I work with have definitely started depending on me less. They just kind of sideline me now. It's like being picked last for dodgeball all over again. Dodgeball was the worst, honestly. I always got hit right in the face with those red rubber balls. They made that horrible *thwack* sound, you know? And they smelled like old tires. My brother used to work at a tire shop and his hands permanently smelled like rubber and grease, no matter how much of that orange pumice soap he used. That soap is amazing, though, it feels like washing your hands with wet sand... 

Wait, did that answer the question? I feel like I'm repeating myself a little bit.
Are you feeling like your difficulties with organization, focus, and interrupting others are significantly interfering with your ability to succeed in school or run your shop?

Yeah, I mean... I feel like we just talked about this, right? But yes, it's definitely messing things up. Like I was saying, I completely missed those required steps for my program because I just couldn't keep it all organized, and now my financial aid is totally at risk. Which is just... ugh. I don't even want to think about having to pay out of pocket. Have you seen the price of textbooks lately? It's criminal! I had to buy this one textbook for a class last semester, and it was like two hundred dollars, and we literally only used it twice. Twice! And it was so heavy I felt like I was lugging around a brick. I tried to sell it back to the bookstore, but they only offered me like twelve dollars for it. Twelve dollars! You can't even buy a decent lunch for twelve dollars anymore. I went to that sandwich place down the street yesterday and a turkey club was fifteen bucks. And they skimped on the bacon! If you're going to charge fifteen dollars for a sandwich, it better have, like, a mountain of bacon on it. Bacon is so good though. My dad used to make it every Sunday morning, and the whole house would smell like it for hours... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, school and the shop. Yeah, so the financial aid thing is a huge mess. And then with the shop, like I mentioned, the people I work on projects with are definitely depending on me less. They just don't trust me with the important stuff anymore, which is really frustrating. But yeah, it's definitely interfering with everything. Did I already say all this? I feel like I'm having déjà vu. Déjà vu is so weird, isn't it? It's like a glitch in the matrix...
Do you find yourself having trouble with organization and focus in all parts of your life, or is it mainly just with school and your shop?

Um, all parts of my life? I mean, I guess I'm not really sure if it's *everywhere*. Like, obviously school and the shop are the big ones right now. But... I don't know, maybe? I haven't really thought about it outside of that. It's hard to tell because my room is always kind of a mess, but I feel like everyone's room is a mess at twenty-one, right? My mom always used to complain about it. She bought me these clear plastic storage bins once, thinking it would help me organize my clothes. But they smelled so strongly of that weird factory plastic smell. You know that smell? Like a new shower curtain, but worse. I had to leave them out on the balcony for a week just to air them out, and then a bird built a nest in one of them! A literal nest. It was a pigeon, I think. Pigeons are so gross, they're just rats with wings. But the babies were kind of cute in a really ugly way, all pink and fuzzy. I tried to feed them breadcrumbs, but then I read online that bread is actually terrible for birds, it makes their stomachs swell up or something. So I bought this special seed mix, but the bag had a hole in it and I spilled it all over the hallway carpet...

Wait, sorry. What were you asking? Is it just school and the shop? Yeah, I don't really know if it happens other places. I haven't really noticed.
Have you always had trouble with organization and focus, or is this something that started happening more recently?

Um, always? No, not always. I mean, it's been a real problem for about... I'd say two years and two months? Yeah, that sounds right. It started right around the time I changed schools and had to start managing the business program and my accessories shop at the same time, but with way less structure. Before that, things were pretty okay. But changing schools was such a huge deal. The new campus is massive, like, you practically need a map and a compass just to find the cafeteria. And the cafeteria food? Don't even get me started. They have this pizza that tastes like cardboard with ketchup on it. I swear, they must buy it in bulk from some discount warehouse. Speaking of bulk, I tried to buy beads for my accessories shop in bulk once to save money, but they sent me the wrong colors. I ordered turquoise and they sent me this weird, sickly green color. It looked like pea soup. Have you ever had pea soup? My grandma used to make it, and she'd put these giant chunks of ham in it. I hate ham. It's too salty, you know? It always makes me super thirsty afterward, and then I end up drinking like a gallon of water and having to pee every five minutes... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, when did it start. Yeah, so about two years and two months ago, when I switched schools and started juggling the program and the shop without anyone breathing down my neck.
Have you always had some level of trouble with organization and focus, even when you were younger?

Well, I mean, if you're talking about being younger... I guess my mom still has all these old notes from my elementary school teachers. They were always writing home saying I was out of my seat constantly, or that I'd just start talking before anyone even called on me. And they always complained that I rushed through group activities, even when I totally understood the work. I just wanted to get it done, you know? Like, why sit there forever if you already know how to do it? 

It reminds me of this one time in third grade, we had to make these dioramas out of shoeboxes. Remember those? You had to bring in a shoebox and cover it in construction paper. My mom bought me this really cool metallic paper, it was so shiny. But it was impossible to glue down! The glue would just slide right off it. I ended up using an entire roll of Scotch tape, and it looked terrible. My diorama was supposed to be the rainforest, but it ended up looking like a shiny silver trash can with some plastic monkeys taped inside. I loved those little plastic animals, though. I used to collect them from those quarter machines at the grocery store. The grocery store by our old house had the best machines. They had one that dispensed these sticky hands that you could slap against the wall, but they always got covered in fuzz and hair after like five minutes. My mom hated those. She threw one away once because it got stuck to the ceiling fan and left a grease mark...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being younger. Yeah, so the teachers definitely noticed I was always out of my seat and rushing through stuff and talking out of turn. But the organization and focus part... I don't know, maybe it wasn't as big of a deal back then because they sort of managed everything for us?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Um, restless? Yeah, definitely. Like, especially if I have to sit through a long lecture or a study group meeting for the business program. I don't even realize I'm doing it half the time, but my leg will just be bouncing a mile a minute. Or I'll be clicking a pen over and over, or digging around in my bag messing with the beads or key rings from my shop. The key rings are actually really fun to play with, I get these star-shaped ones that are holographic. They look so cool in the sunlight. I tried to take a video of them for my shop's Instagram, but the lighting in my apartment is awful. The windows face this brick wall of the building next door, so I barely get any natural light. It's so depressing. I tried buying a ring light, but it was super cheap and broke after like three days. The stand just snapped right in half. I guess that's what I get for buying it off some random website instead of a real store. But real stores are so expensive! Like, have you seen the price of camera equipment lately? It's insane. My friend bought a fancy camera to take pictures of her dog—she has this really fluffy Pomeranian named Waffles. He's adorable, but he barks at literally everything. A leaf blows past the window? Bark. The mailman drops off a package? Bark. It's cute for about five minutes, and then you just want to put earplugs in...

Wait, sorry, I lost track. What did you ask? Oh, right, fidgety. Yeah, so in lectures or meetings, my leg is always bouncing or I'm clicking a pen or playing with my shop stuff before I even notice I'm doing it.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go or have an inability to engage in activities quietly?

Um, constantly on the go? Not really. I don't feel like I'm driven by a motor or anything. And doing things quietly... I mean, I think I can do things quietly? Like, just the other night I was trying to quietly string some new bracelets for the shop while my roommate was sleeping. She works these crazy night shifts at a bakery downtown. Have you ever been to that bakery on 4th street? They make these amazing croissants. The chocolate ones are the best, but you have to get there by like 7 AM or they sell out completely. I tried to make croissants once from scratch, and it was a total disaster. You have to fold the butter into the dough like a million times, and it has to stay freezing cold. But my apartment is always so hot because the radiator is broken and the landlord refuses to fix it. He's this grumpy old guy who always wears the exact same plaid shirt. I swear he must have a closet full of them, like a cartoon character. You know how cartoon characters never change clothes? Like SpongeBob, always in the square pants. I used to watch SpongeBob every single morning before school, eating those sugary cereals that turn the milk weird colors... 

Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, being on the go and not being quiet. Yeah, no, I don't really relate to that. I can just chill out and do my beadwork quietly when I need to. I definitely don't feel like I'm always running around.
Did you have any of these issues with organization, focus, or interrupting others when you were a child?

Wait, didn't we just talk about this? Yeah, I'm pretty sure I said... um, my mom kept all those old notes from my elementary school teachers. They were always complaining that I was constantly out of my seat, or that I'd just start blurting things out and talking before anyone even called on me. And they always said I rushed through group activities, even when I totally understood the material. I just wanted to get it over with, you know? Like, if you know the answer, why drag it out? 

It's like when you're watching a movie and you already know who the killer is in the first ten minutes. Why sit through the next two hours? My roommate and I were watching this true crime documentary the other night, and it was so obvious it was the husband. It's always the husband, right? But she made me watch all four episodes anyway. We ordered a pizza, though, so it wasn't a total loss. We got it from that place on the corner that puts the tiny pepperonis on it that curl up into little grease cups. I love those. But they forgot the garlic dipping sauce, which is literally the best part. I called them to ask for it, and the guy on the phone was so rude. He acted like I was asking him to personally deliver a bar of gold or something. I mean, it's just garlic sauce... 

Wait, sorry. Yeah, so as a kid, definitely the interrupting and the being out of my seat and rushing through things. That was all in those notes my mom kept.
Did you have a lot of energy and run around a lot when you were a kid?

Um, run around a lot? I don't know if I ran around more than other kids, but I definitely felt... like, even if I wasn't actually running, I always felt this weird buzzing inside? Like my whole body was just humming and I needed to move somehow. Especially when I was supposed to be sitting still and listening to the teacher. It was physical, you know? Like this itchy feeling under my skin if I didn't move. 

Actually, it kind of felt like when you drink way too much caffeine on an empty stomach. I did that yesterday, actually. I had this massive iced coffee from the place near my apartment—the one with the ridiculous paper straws that dissolve in your drink after like two sips. I hate those straws. I get that they're trying to save the turtles, which is great, I love turtles. I saw a sea turtle once when my family went to Florida for spring break in high school. We went snorkeling, and the water was so clear. But my brother got completely sunburned on his back because he refused to wear sunscreen. He looked like a lobster for the rest of the trip and complained the whole time. He's always complaining about something, though. Like, last week he called me just to complain about his new car... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, running around as a kid. Yeah, so I don't know about running around, but I definitely had that buzzing feeling where I just needed to move, especially when I had to sit still.
Do you think your difficulties with organization, focus, and interrupting others have significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?

Um, yeah, I guess so. I mean, it's definitely causing some major stress right now. Because I keep missing these required steps for my program, my financial aid is actually at risk. If I lose that, I don't even know what I'll do. My roommate said she could maybe spot me for rent, but I hate borrowing money. It always makes things weird, you know? Like this one time I lent my friend Sarah twenty bucks for concert tickets, and she literally avoided me for a month instead of just saying she didn't have it yet. The concert was for this indie band that plays all their songs on vintage instruments. The lead singer plays a theremin. Have you ever seen someone play a theremin? It's so cool, they just wave their hands in the air and it makes these spooky sci-fi noises. I tried to look up how much one costs online because I thought it would be fun to learn, but they're insanely expensive. And honestly, where would I even put it in my apartment? I already have boxes of beads everywhere for my shop. 

Which, actually, that's another thing. The people I work with on shop projects... they've definitely started depending on me less. Like, they'll just do things themselves instead of asking me because I guess I interrupt or get distracted too much. It sucks, but I get it. Wait, did I answer your question? Yeah, the financial aid thing and the shop projects... it's definitely messing things up.
Did you experience difficulties with organization, focus, or interrupting others before you were a teenager?

Wait, didn't I just tell you about this? Like literally a few minutes ago? Yeah, I'm pretty sure I mentioned the notes... my mom kept all those old notes from my elementary school teachers. They were always writing home saying I was constantly getting out of my seat, or blurting out answers before they even called on me. And they said I'd rush through all the group activities, even though I actually understood the work perfectly fine. I just wanted to get it done. 

It's like when you're doing a puzzle and you already know what the picture is going to look like. Why spend hours finding all the little blue sky pieces? My roommate loves puzzles. She has this massive 2,000-piece one of a castle taking up our entire dining table right now. We haven't been able to eat there for a week. We've just been eating on the couch, which is fine, but I dropped a piece of pepperoni under the cushion yesterday and I still can't find it. It's driving me crazy because I know it's going to attract bugs. We had ants last summer and it was a nightmare. They were coming in through this tiny crack by the window... 

Anyway, yeah, sorry. I already told you about the elementary school notes, right? The talking and being out of my seat and stuff. That was definitely before I was a teenager.
Did you often feel the need to run around or engage in physical activity as a child?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally the first thing we talked about? I swear we just went over this... the whole running around thing. 

Yeah, I mean, I don't know about actually running, but I told you about that weird buzzing feeling, right? Like my body is just humming and I have to move somehow, even if I'm not going anywhere. Especially when I'm supposed to just sit there and listen. It's like this physical itch. 

It's actually kind of like how my dog acts right before a thunderstorm. My family has this golden retriever back home, Buster, and he can sense the pressure dropping or whatever before it even starts raining. He just paces back and forth in the living room, whining and trying to dig into the carpet. My mom had to buy this special thundershirt for him that wraps around him really tight. It's supposed to make them feel safe, like a hug, but honestly, he still looks pretty miserable when he wears it. He just sits there looking like a stuffed sausage. I miss him so much. I wanted to bring him to my apartment, but my landlord has this strict no-pets policy, which is so stupid because the girl down the hall definitely has a cat. I can smell the litter box every time I walk past her door. It's gross. I don't understand how people can live with that smell... 

But yeah, anyway, the buzzing feeling. I already said that, right? I just feel like I need to move.

doctor.intent: identify the patient's chief complaint
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Organization_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time—my supplies, due dates, receipts, and assignment notes all end up in piles and I don't know what to do first.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for the chief complaint (what brings me in today). The prompt specifies that on the first reply, I must return the item whose key is my chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S005.

patient.answer:
Hi! So, um, I came in because I feel like I just cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Like, my supplies, my due dates, receipts, assignment notes... they all just end up in these giant piles. 

I actually make resin keychains and stuff for the shop, and I just bought this really amazing holographic glitter online. The shipping was incredibly fast, which is so weird because usually the post office takes forever, right? Last time I ordered from them, they sent my package to the completely wrong state, and I had to spend like an hour on hold with customer service just listening to that awful elevator music. 

But anyway, yeah, everything for school and the shop is just in piles everywhere in my room, and I just stand there looking at it all and I honestly don't know what to do first.

inference.note: Added potential attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (F90.0) and unspecified attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (F90.8) due to reported disorganization and difficulty prioritizing tasks, and other symptoms such as distractibility (e.g., discussing the holographic glitter and shipping issues) which may indicate cognitive impairment or attention issues (R41.8).

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's disorganization is causing significant distress
doctor.question: How stressful does it feel for you to be surrounded by these piles of schoolwork and shop supplies?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the emotional impact (stress level) of the disorganization, which is not directly covered by any specific symptom profile item, as they focus on the manifestations of the symptoms, impairment, onset, or duration.

patient.answer:
Um, honestly? I'm not really sure. I don't know if I'd say it's stressful, exactly, because I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess I just kind of stare at it. 

Like, the other day I was digging through the pile on my desk to find a shipping receipt, and I actually found this old mood ring I bought at a street fair when I was like, twelve. Do you remember those? The ones that turn blue when you're happy and black when you're stressed? It's like when you're doing a puzzle and you already know what the picture is going to look like. Why spend hours finding all the little blue sky pieces? My roommate loves puzzles. She has this massive 2,000-piece one of a castle taking up our entire dining table right now. We haven't been able to eat there for a week. We've just been eating on the couch, which is fine, but I dropped a piece of pepperoni under the cushion yesterday and I still can't find it. It's driving me crazy because I know it's going to attract bugs. We had ants last summer and it was a nightmare. They were coming in through this tiny crack by the window... 

Anyway, yeah, sorry. I already told you about the elementary school notes, right? The talking and being out of my seat and stuff. That was definitely before I was a teenager.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of hyperactivity in childhood
doctor.question: Did you often feel the need to run around or engage in physical activity as a child?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: Even when I'm not actually going anywhere, I feel like my body is buzzing and I need to be moving, especially when I'm supposed to sit still and listen.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about running around or engaging in excessive physical activity during childhood, which directly matches the symptom of feeling restless or running about/climbing inappropriately.

patient.answer:
Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally the first thing we talked about? I swear we just went over this... the whole running around thing. 

Yeah, I mean, I don't know about actually running, but I told you about that weird buzzing feeling, right? Like my body is just humming and I have to move somehow, even if I'm not going anywhere. Especially when I'm supposed to just sit there and listen. It's like this physical itch. 

It's actually kind of like how my dog acts right before a thunderstorm. My family has this golden retriever back home, Buster, and he can sense the pressure dropping or whatever before it even starts raining. He just paces back and forth in the living room, whining and trying to dig into the carpet. My mom had to buy this special thundershirt for him that wraps around him really tight. It's supposed to make them feel safe, like a hug, but honestly, he still looks pretty miserable when he wears it. He just sits there looking like a stuffed sausage. I miss him so much. I wanted to bring him to my apartment, but my landlord has this strict no-pets policy, which is so stupid because the girl down the hall definitely has a cat. I can smell the litter box every time I walk past her door. It's gross. I don't understand how people can live with that smell... 

But yeah, anyway, the buzzing feeling. I already said that, right? I just feel like I need to move.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms, including difficulties with organization, focus, interrupting others, restlessness, and fidgetiness, have been persistent across their life, particularly worsening over the past two years. These symptoms significantly impact their daily functioning, relationships, and academic performance, aligning closely with the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), predominantly inattentive type, though the presence of hyperactive symptoms in childhood and some current symptoms suggest a consideration of combined presentation. However, the inattentive symptoms are more prominently described and have caused significant impairment.
